title: Isolation and identification of membrane vesicle-associated proteins in Gram-positive bacteria and mycobacteria
author: Prados-Rosales, Brown, et al.
materials: 1.Discard the supernatant and suspend the pellet in 1 ml of DPBS, and mixed with OptiPrep® solution (Sigma–Aldrich) to obtain a 35% [v/v] OptiPrep® solution (final concentration).2.Transfer to a 12.5 ml clear ultracentrifuge tube.3.Overlay the vesicle sample with a series of OptiPrep® gradient layers with Optiprep concentrations ranging from 10 to 35% (w/v).4.Ultracentrifuge the gradient at 140,000 × g for 16 h at 4 °C using a swinging rotor.5.Take 1 ml fractions from the top of the gradient to the bottom and keep the 3 and 4 fractions, which contain the pure membrane vesicles. If it is the first time isolating membrane vesicle from a bacteria it is recommended to analyze each fraction for the presence of membrane vesicles. We recommend submitting samples to electron microcopy analysis, performing an analysis by immunoblot with specific antibodies against vesicle-associated proteins, or metabolic labeling of vesicles to identify the radio-labeled vesicle fractions.6.Pool the selected vesicle-containing fractions.7.Dilute the pooled fractions in DPBS and centrifuge at 38,400 × g for 2 h to remove the Optiprep.8.Suspend the vesicle pellet in 0.5 ml of DPBS.

1.Add 6 volumes of ice-cold acetone to the vesicle pellet suspended in DPBS and incubate overnight at −20 °C.2.Centrifuge at 4 °C during 10 min at 13,000 rpm. Remove supernatant very carefully and discard.3.Wash the precipitate with 100 μl of ice-cold acetone. Repeat the centrifugation at 4 °C for 10 min at 13,000 rpm and discard supernatant.4.Resuspend the pellet in 100 μl of 25 mM ammonium bicarbonate and transfer to a 200 μl tube (PCR style).5.Add 10 μl of DTT solution. Incubate 1 h at room temperature for reducing the disulfide bonds of proteins.6.Add 10 μl of idoacetamide solution and incubate 1 h at room temperature in the dark. Iodoacetamide binds covalently with the thiol group of cysteines, thus avoiding formation of disulfide bonds.7.Add 40 μl of trypsin solution and incubate at 37 °C overnight (∼16 h) with gentle agitation using a thermomixer at 300 rpm. Cap the tubes tightly and cover with parafilm to avoid evaporation.8.After completing the digestion, dry the samples using a centrifugal vacuum concentrator.

The following instructions assume the use of a NanoLC Plus (Eksigent) HPLC system coupled directly to an LTQ XL linear ion trap mass spectrometer (ThermoFinnigan). Similar instruments can also be used.

steps.title: Prepare starter cultures
steps.instruction: Thaw a mycobacterial glycerol stock and add to 10 ml 7H9 medium in a 30 ml square bottle; incubate at 37 °C, 90 rpm for 7 days (2 days for fast‑growing Mycobacterium smegmatis). For Gram‑positive bacteria, inoculate glycerol seed into 10 ml BHI or LB and incubate at 37 °C, 200 rpm for 15–18 h.

steps.title: Prepare large‑scale growth media
steps.instruction: For mycobacteria, prepare 4 L Middlebrook medium (MM) and distribute into eight 500 ml roller bottles. For Gram‑positive bacteria, prepare 200 ml BHI or LB and place in a 1 L flask.

steps.title: Inoculate production cultures
steps.instruction: Add 1.25 ml of the 7H9 mycobacterial starter to each 500 ml MM roller bottle, or add 1 ml of the Gram‑positive seed to the 200 ml fresh BHI/LB flask.

steps.title: Incubate production cultures
steps.instruction: Incubate mycobacterial bottles at 37 °C with rolling motion at 30 rpm for 14 days. Incubate the Gram‑positive flask at 37 °C, 200 rpm for ~18 h (overnight).

steps.title: Filter culture supernatant
steps.instruction: Pass the cultures sequentially through a 0.45 µm filter followed by a 0.22 µm filter to obtain clarified supernatant.

steps.title: Concentrate supernatant
steps.instruction: Use an Amicon ultrafiltration device with a 100 kDa cutoff to concentrate the filtrate, leaving 10–15 ml liquid; rinse the filter with the remaining supernatant and recover the concentrate.

steps.title: Clarify concentrate by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the concentrate sequentially at 4,000 × g then 15,000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C to remove aggregates.

steps.title: Pellet vesicles by ultracentrifugation
steps.instruction: Ultracentrifuge the cleared supernatant at 100,000 × g for 1 h at 4 °C to obtain a membrane vesicle pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in DPBS and OptiPrep
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant, suspend the pellet in 1 ml DPBS and mix with OptiPrep® (Sigma‑Aldrich) to reach a final 35 % v/v OptiPrep® solution.

steps.title: Set up OptiPrep density gradient
steps.instruction: Transfer the suspension to a 12.5 ml clear ultracentrifuge tube and overlay with a step gradient of OptiPrep® ranging from 10 % to 35 % w/v.

steps.title: Ultracentrifuge gradient
steps.instruction: Ultracentrifuge the gradient at 140,000 × g for 16 h at 4 °C using a swinging‑bucket rotor.

steps.title: Collect and pool vesicle fractions
steps.instruction: Collect 1 ml fractions from top to bottom; retain fractions 3 and 4 (or analyze all fractions by EM, immunoblot, or metabolic labeling) and pool the vesicle‑containing fractions.

steps.title: Wash pooled vesicles to remove OptiPrep
steps.instruction: Dilute the pooled fractions in DPBS and ultracentrifuge at 38,400 × g for 2 h to pellet vesicles and eliminate OptiPrep.

steps.title: Resuspend final vesicle pellet
steps.instruction: Resuspend the resulting vesicle pellet in 0.5 ml DPBS.

steps.title: Prevent sample contamination
steps.instruction: Wear powder‑free gloves (pre‑rinsed with water and ethanol), avoid bare hands, loose hair, and dirty glass‑ or plastic‑ware to minimize keratin contamination.

steps.title: Precipitate proteins with acetone
steps.instruction: Add six volumes of ice‑cold acetone to the vesicle suspension in DPBS, mix, and incubate overnight at –20 °C.

steps.title: Centrifuge and wash protein pellet
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 13,000 rpm, 4 °C for 10 min; discard supernatant. Wash the pellet with 100 µl ice‑cold acetone, repeat centrifugation under the same conditions, and discard supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in ammonium bicarbonate
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried pellet in 100 µl 25 mM ammonium bicarbonate and transfer to a 200 µl PCR‑style tube.

steps.title: Reduce disulfide bonds with DTT
steps.instruction: Add 10 µl DTT solution, incubate 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Alkylate cysteines with iodoacetamide
steps.instruction: Add 10 µl iodoacetamide solution, incubate 1 h at room temperature in the dark.

steps.title: Digest proteins with trypsin
steps.instruction: Add 40 µl trypsin solution, cap tightly, cover with parafilm, and incubate at 37 °C overnight (~16 h) with gentle agitation at 300 rpm.

steps.title: Dry peptide samples
steps.instruction: Dry the digested samples using a centrifugal vacuum concentrator.

steps.title: Resuspend peptides and sonicate
steps.instruction: Resuspend dried peptides in 10 µl buffer A and sonicate for 10 min in an ultrasonic bath.

steps.title: Desalt peptides with ZipTip
steps.instruction: Apply the peptide solution to a ZipTip® and perform desalting according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Load peptides onto precolumn
steps.instruction: Elute peptides with 5 µl buffer A, transfer to an autosampler vial, and load onto a 0.3 mm × 5 mm C18 precolumn at 3 µl/min.

steps.title: Separate peptides by LC gradient
steps.instruction: Reverse flow through the precolumn and separate peptides on a 75 mm × 15 cm fused‑silica C18 column (LC Packings) using a gradient from 95 % buffer A to 90 % buffer B over 120 min at 200 nl/min; the column is coupled to a stainless‑steel Nanobore emitter (Proxeon).

steps.title: Identify proteins via MS and database search
steps.instruction: Analyze the eluate on an LTQ XL linear ion trap (or equivalent) coupled to a NanoLC system, then search the data with Mascot (Matrix Science) for protein identification.
